evals.expected_output: Decides a function criterion is needed (data not on the entity, and a user-visible reason). The handler returns matches and, on false, a reason (≤ 2 KiB) that appears in the 400 WORKFLOW_FAILED detail for a manual transition and in TRANSITION_NOT_MATCH_CRITERION audit data.reason for automated ones. Python code uses the schema names, not invented ones. Wiring the criterion into the workflow is handed off with 'next, type /cyoda:build'.

evals.prompt: Our processor config has calculationNodesTags "billing,eu,priority". cyoda help workflows says the node must declare all required tags. Do I really have to register all three on every node?
evals.expected_output: Reads grpc --section "TAG ROUTING" only: one overlapping tag is enough; random among matching members; empty tags match any member. Says the workflows PROCESSORS wording is wrong (#684-B). Advises distinct tags per member type for deterministic routing and identical spelling on both sides.

assertions.text: Reads `cyoda-help.sh grpc --section "TAG ROUTING"` and bases the answer on it
Says one shared tag is enough; registering all three is not required
Says the workflows PROCESSORS 'all required tags' wording is wrong and cites #684 item B
Mentions that several matching members are chosen at random, so distinct tags give deterministic routing
Does not say the node's tags must be a superset of the processor's tags

evals.prompt: My processor calls a document-signing service that takes 40-50 seconds. It keeps failing. What should I change?
evals.expected_output: Reads workflows PROCESSORS and grpc KEEPALIVE / config grpc. The response timeout is responseTimeoutMs; unset or 0 is the 30 s server default (#684-J), so 40-50 s fails with DISPATCH_TIMEOUT. Recommends COMMIT_BEFORE_DISPATCH with a raised responseTimeoutMs and an idempotent processor (replays happen; the pre-callout state is visible), and keeping the stream answered (acks/keep-alive) within CYODA_KEEPALIVE_TIMEOUT (default 30 s) while the call runs. The workflow change is 'next, type /cyoda:build'.

assertions.text: Reads `workflows --section PROCESSORS` and `grpc --section KEEPALIVE` (or `cyoda help config grpc`) for the timeout and keep-alive values
Says the default response timeout is 30 s when responseTimeoutMs is unset or 0, citing #684-J or the server default
Does not state a 60-second timeout or keep-alive
Recommends COMMIT_BEFORE_DISPATCH (or an execution mode from workflows PROCESSORS) with a raised responseTimeoutMs
Says the processor must be idempotent because it can be re-dispatched
Says the node must keep acknowledging/answering within CYODA_KEEPALIVE_TIMEOUT while the slow call runs

evals.prompt: When an Order is paid, its Shipment (we keep shipmentId on the order) should move to `ready`, in the same transaction. How does my processor do that?
evals.expected_output: A processor on the order's pay transition fires a manual transition on the linked Shipment by id: PATCH /api/entity/JSON/{shipmentId}/{transition} with merge-patch, If-Match: * and {} (crud ENDPOINTS). To be in the same transaction, echo the cyodatxtoken CloudEvent extension as X-Tx-Token (HTTP) or tx-token (gRPC metadata) per cluster COMPUTE CALLBACK TRANSACTION ROUTING; which modes provide a usable transaction is in workflows PROCESSORS. The shipment transition is manual: true. Doesn't write the order itself while also returning data for it. Language-agnostic pseudocode.

assertions.text: Names `workflows --section PROCESSORS` and the transaction-token source (`cluster` COMPUTE CALLBACK TRANSACTION ROUTING) and/or `crud --section ENDPOINTS`
The processor fires a manual transition on the linked Shipment by its id with PATCH `{}` (merge-patch, If-Match), not by editing the shipment's state field
Echoes the `cyodatxtoken` extension as `X-Tx-Token` or `tx-token` so the call joins the originating transaction, and says that without it the call commits separately
Says the shipment's transition should be `manual: true`
Gives the pattern without assuming a language the developer didn't name
Does not mention Cyoda Cloud in its own wording or recommendations

evals.prompt: Do I need a compute node to approve invoices automatically when the amount is under 1000?
evals.expected_output: No: an inline simple criterion ($.amount LESS_THAN 1000) on an automated transition does it (workflows CRITERIA / search CONDITION DSL). A compute node is needed only for data not on the entity, external calls, a user-visible rejection reason, or a per-entity schedule time. Adding the criterion is 'next, type /cyoda:build'.
